label: prf:c5-involution-leibniz-decomposition
title: Proof of c5 involution leibniz decomposition
html:
Proof. Proof of c5 involution leibniz decomposition

Proof sketch

Step 1: bar involution and the averaged crossing

The Hecke algebra H_n(q) carries the bar involution \overline{\,\,}, a \mathbb{Z}-linear anti-ring-automorphism defined by:

\overline{q} = q^{-1}, \quad \overline{\sigma_i} = \sigma_i^{-1}.

Using the Hecke quadratic \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 (where h = q - q^{-1}), we have \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h.

The bar-invariant projector is P_{\text{avg}} = (1 + \overline{\,\,})/2. Its action on \sigma_i gives:

P_{\text{avg}}(\sigma_i) \;=\; \frac{\sigma_i + \overline{\sigma_i}}{2}
\;=\; \frac{\sigma_i + \sigma_i^{-1}}{2}
\;=\; \frac{\sigma_i + \sigma_i - h}{2}
\;=\; \sigma_i - \frac{h}{2}.

This is the averaged crossing operator \sigma_{\text{avg}} used in the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 braid recipe.

Step 2: averaged crossings in the typed braid

From prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic, the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 proton braid uses ONE averaged \sigma_1:

\mathcal{B}_p \;=\; \sigma_0 \cdot (\sigma_1 - \tfrac{h}{2}\mathbf{1})
\;=\; \sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_{1,\text{avg}}.

The typed neutron braid uses TWO averaged crossings (one at \sigma_0, one at \sigma_1):

\mathcal{B}_n \;=\; (\sigma_0 - \tfrac{h}{2}\mathbf{1}) \cdot (\sigma_1 - h\mathbf{1})
\;=\; \sigma_{0,\text{avg}} \cdot \sigma_1^{-1}.

Each averaged crossing contributes a factor of h/2 = 1/2 at the specific position where it appears.

Step 3: Leibniz propagation to higher rungs

The categorical Markov-trace expansion of the typed braid in powers of h generates the single-wrap baseline (Form A) plus the precision-ladder corrections. The h/2 contributions from averaged positions propagate via the Leibniz product expansion:

\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_n - \mathcal{B}_p) \;=\; \mathrm{net}(n) - \mathrm{net}(p)
\;=\; \frac{h^2}{2} - h
\;=\; \frac{h(h-2)}{2}.

The h^2/2 term is the product of TWO averaged-crossing h/2 contributions (the neutron has two such positions). The h/2 generates the 1/2 in \Delta(\mathrm{net}).

For higher rungs N = k \geq 4 of the precision ladder, the expansion of \mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta) in b \cdot \hbar_q^2 produces coefficients with two distinct categorical origins:

  • Pure-\sigma contributions: from non-averaged positions in the braid. These factor through \sigma^p \cdot b^{2m} combinatorics. At the silver ratio (\sigma-eigenvalues = 1 \pm \sqrt{2} via the Hecke quadratic prop:silver-ratio-beta-decay-null), these reduce to Pell-Lucas-clean rationals.

  • Averaged-crossing contributions: from positions where \sigma_{\text{avg}} acts. These pick up the 1/2 fingerprint of P_{\text{avg}}. At the silver ratio they give rationals with a 1/2 component that is Pell-Lucas-incompatible.

Step 4: rung-by-rung classification

Sequential extraction of c_k via R(q_0) = \prod_k (1 + c_k b^k \hbar_q^{2k}) gives:

c_k Closed form Origin At silver ratio
c_3 -2 J_{\text{Hopf}}(q=1), pure inter-block -2 (clean)
c_4 c_3 \cdot b^4 \sigma^p \cdot b^{2m} pure -49/32 = -a_3^2/2^5 (clean)
c_5 \boxed{-b^2 - 1/2} \sigma + averaging -11/8 (1/2 OUTLIER)
c_6 c_3^2 \cdot b^2 \sigma^p \cdot b^{2m} pure 7/2 = a_3/2 (clean)
c_7 c_3^3 pure \sigma powers -8 (clean integer)

The c_5 outlier is structurally distinct because \sigma_{\text{avg}} contributions at rung 5 are dominant — at all other rungs in [3, 7], the pure-\sigma contributions dominate and the averaging contributions are subdominant. □

Proofs (Lean \leftrightarrow paper bridge)

Every substantive Lean theorem in c5-involution-leibniz-decomposition.lean has both a narrative proof here and a sorry-free Lean proof.

Hoefsmit–Quantum-2 identity

Theorem (Lean: hoefsmit_b_squared_eq_one_minus_inv_quantum_two_squared). For all q \neq 0 in \mathbb{R},

b^2(q) \;=\; \frac{q^4 + q^2 + 1}{(q^2 + 1)^2} \;=\; 1 - \frac{1}{[2]_q^2}.

Proof. Multiply both sides by [2]_q^2 = (q + q^{-1})^2: (q^2 + 1)^2 = q^2 \cdot (q + q^{-1})^2 since (q+q^{-1})^2 = (q^2+1)^2/q^2. So b^2 = (q^4+q^2+1)/(q^2[2]_q^2). Multiply numerator and denominator of b^2 by 1/q^2: b^2 = (q^2 + 1 + q^{-2})/[2]_q^2 = ([2]_q^2 - 1)/[2]_q^2 = 1 - 1/[2]_q^2 since q^2 + 1 + q^{-2} = (q+q^{-1})^2 - 1 = [2]_q^2 - 1. Lean tactic: field_simp; ring. \square

Corollary (Lean: c5_decomposition_via_quantum_two). c_5(q) = -3/2 + 1/[2]_q^2. Proof. Substitute b^2 = 1 - 1/[2]_q^2 into c_5 = -b^2 - 1/2: c_5 = -(1 - 1/[2]_q^2) - 1/2 = -3/2 + 1/[2]_q^2. \square

Classical-QOU limit + Wedderburn identification

Theorem (Lean: c5_classical_limit_eq_neg_five_quarters). c_5(q = 1) = -5/4. Proof. At q = 1: [2]_q = 2, so [2]_q^2 = 4, 1/[2]_q^2 = 1/4, c_5(1) = -3/2 + 1/4 = -5/4. By norm_num. \square

Theorem (Lean: c5_classical_eq_wedderburn_nonsign_dim_half). c_5(1) = -(\dim V_{(3)} + \dim V_{(2,1)})/2 + 1/4 = -5/4. Proof. The Wedderburn decomposition of \mathbb{C}[S_3] has three irreps with dimensions 1 (V_{(3)}), 2 (V_{(2,1)}), 1 (V_{(1,1,1)}). The non-sign sum is 1 + 2 = 3; half is 3/2. So -3/2 = -(\dim V_{(3)} + \dim V_{(2,1)})/2. Combine with 1/4 = 1/[2]_q^2 at q=1 to get -5/4. \square

Silver-ratio identity

Lemma (Lean: quantumTwo_at_silver_ratio_squared). [2]_q^2 = 8 at q = 1 + \sqrt 2. Proof. [2]_{1+\sqrt 2} = (1+\sqrt 2) + 1/(1+\sqrt 2) = (1+\sqrt 2) + (\sqrt 2 - 1) = 2\sqrt 2. So [2]_q^2 = 8. Lean tactic:

field_simp; ring_nf; linarith [Real.mul_self_sqrt (by norm_num : (2:ℝ) ≥ 0)]

\square

Theorem (Lean: b_squared_at_silver_ratio). b^2(1 + \sqrt 2) = 7/8. Proof. From Hoefsmit–Quantum-2 + the lemma above: b^2 = 1 - 1/[2]_q^2 = 1 - 1/8 = 7/8. \square

Corollary (Lean: c5_at_silver_ratio_is_minus_11_over_8). c_5(\mathrm{silver}) = -11/8. Proof. From the c_5 closed form + the silver-ratio identity: c_5 = -3/2 + 1/8 = -12/8 + 1/8 = -11/8. Numerator 11 is inert in \mathbb{Z}[1+\sqrt 2] (not in Pell-Lucas closure) — the c_5 outlier fingerprint. \square

c_5 in terms of Hecke skein h

Lemma (Lean: quantum_two_squared_eq_skein_squared_plus_four). For all q \neq 0: [2]_q^2 = h^2 + 4 where h = q - q^{-1}. Proof. (q + q^{-1})^2 = q^2 + 2 + q^{-2} and (q - q^{-1})^2 + 4 = (q^2 - 2 + q^{-2}) + 4 = q^2 + 2 + q^{-2}. Equal. \square

Theorem (Lean: c5_as_function_of_skein). c_5(q) = -3/2 + 1/(h^2 + 4) where h = q - q^{-1}. Proof. Substitute the previous lemma into the closed form c_5 = -3/2 + 1/[2]_q^2. \square

c_5 as a rational map over \mathbb{R}

Proposition (Lean: c5RationalMap_at_skein_eq_c5Decomposition). c5RationalMap(h(q)) = c5Decomposition(q). Proof. Direct rewrite via c5_as_function_of_skein. \square

Proposition (Lean: h_sq_plus_four_pos, h_sq_plus_four_ne_zero). h^2 + 4 > 0 over \mathbb{R}. Proof. h^2 \geq 0; add 4 to get \geq 4 > 0. \square

Proposition (Lean: c5RationalMap_zero/two/one). Three concrete evaluations: c_5(h{=}0) = -5/4, c_5(h{=}2) = -11/8, c_5(h{=}1) = -13/10. Proof. Direct numerical computation via norm_num. \square

Theorem (Lean: c5RationalMap_even h). c_5(-h) = c_5(h) (even function). Proof. (-h)^2 = h^2; substitute. The categorical content of bar-symmetry: c_5 is invariant under bar acting as h \to -h. \square

Theorem (Lean: c5RationalMap_le_neg_five_quarters h). c_5(h) \leq -5/4 for all real h, with equality at h = 0. Proof. h^2 + 4 \geq 4, so 1/(h^2 + 4) \leq 1/4, hence c_5 = -3/2 + 1/(h^2+4) \leq -3/2 + 1/4 = -5/4. \square

Theorem (Lean: c5RationalMap_gt_neg_three_halves h). c_5(h) > -3/2 for all real h. Proof. 1/(h^2 + 4) > 0, so c_5 > -3/2. The bound is approached asymptotically as |h| \to \infty but never reached. \square

Theorem (Lean: c5RationalMap_strict_neg h). c_5(h) < 0 for all real h. Proof. From the upper bound: c_5 \leq -5/4 < 0. \square

Theorem (Lean: c5RationalMap_max_at_zero h). h = 0 achieves the maximum of c_5. Proof. Combine c_5(h) \leq -5/4 with c_5(0) = -5/4. \square

Theorem (Lean: c5OfHSquared_antitone_on_nonneg). c_5 is monotonically decreasing in h^2 on the nonneg domain. Proof. For 0 \leq x \leq y: both x+4 and y+4 are positive, y + 4 \geq x + 4, so 1/(y+4) \leq 1/(x+4), hence c_5(y) \leq c_5(x). \square

Factorization through h^2

Theorem (Lean: c5RationalMap_factor h). c_5(h) = c_5\text{OfHSquared}(h^2). Proof. By definition both unfold to -3/2 + 1/(h^2 + 4). \square

Categorical reading: c_5 factors as

h \xrightarrow{\text{squaring}} h^2 \xrightarrow{\text{rational fn}} c_5

where the first arrow is the canonical anti-sym \to sym projection (IsBarSymmetric.of_mul_antisym) and the second is a bar-symmetric-preserving function. This makes the bar-symmetric structure of c_5 explicit at the level of function composition.

All 24 substantive Lean theorems / definitions in the sibling have narrative proofs above. The Lean file is sorry-free.
